title: Chapter 73: Red and Black
html:
Dilapidated paths crisscrossed like a maze. Afraid of losing them, Chen Ge quickened his pace. After several turns, a squat two-story tenement came into view, and the woman and boy disappeared inside.

The drains around the building reeked. A large notice on the ground floor declared that the original tenants had relocated, and rubbish lay piled in every corner and scattered across the floor.

Questions crowded Chen Ge’s mind as he approached. Their surroundings made it clear they were struggling financially, yet the woman had readily offered a hundred RMB just to get Fan Yu into the Haunted House. She plainly cared for him. Fan Yu, however, treated her with chilling indifference. The only two things he had said at the park were both addressed to Chen Ge. He seemed to despise his aunt.

Is it because of his mental issues, or is something more sinister at work?

Upstairs, Chen Ge discovered that only one unit on the second floor remained occupied. Unlike the rest of the building, its corridor had been swept clean, and laundry hung from poles overhead.

“Is anyone in?” The door was open, but Chen Ge still knocked on the door out of courtesy.

“Coming.”

Footsteps approached from within. The woman visibly startled when she saw Chen Ge.

“Why are you here? Did we cause some damage when we visited the Haunted House?” the woman asked cautiously.

“No, nothing like that. I’m concerned about the boy, and I’d like to ask him something.” The woman showed no inclination to invite him inside, so he added, “I have friends at Jiujiang Medical University. I thought they might be able to help.”

“Thank you, but that’s all right.” She refused without hesitation. Recognizing how intrusive he must seem, Chen Ge added, “I’m honestly not a bad person. Check today’s Jiujiang Morning News.”

When the woman made no move, Chen Ge pulled out his own phone and found an article about his role in solving the Ping An Apartments case.

“Look, I helped the police solve a cold case and received a medal of honor.” Chen Ge handed her the phone. She glanced at the screen. “‘Supernatural Livestreamer Trapped, Rescued by Police’? ‘Haunted House Operator’s Recklessness Nearly Costs Him His Life’?”

“Ignore the headlines. There should be my picture inside the article.”

After a lengthy explanation, the woman finally set aside her suspicions. She returned his phone. “You can come in, then. Just leave the door open.”

“Okay.”

The woman led Chen Ge into the ‘living room,’ a cramped space with a dining table at its center and beds pushed into the corners.

“Forgive the mess. I wasn’t expecting visitors. Would you like something to drink?” Her embarrassment briefly revealed a resemblance to the shy boy.

“That won’t be necessary. I just want to ask some questions about the boy’s parents.” Chen Ge took out his phone to record anything he deemed important.

“It happened so long ago. Why ask now?” Nevertheless, she sat across from Chen Ge and recounted what had happened at Mu Yang High School three years earlier.

Three years earlier, Mu Yang High School had still been an ordinary school. One summer day, rain poured from the sky. Fan Yu’s parents returned from work to find him missing and went back out to search. Fan Yu eventually came home. They never did.

It sounds as if the boy was somehow the reason they disappeared…Chen Ge recorded the key details on his phone, trying to reconstruct the sequence of events.

Fan Yu’s parents came home from work and discovered their son missing. They went out into the downpour to search for him and vanished. Their bodies might now lie at the bottom of Mu Yang High School’s well, with Fan Yu the only witness to what happened.

Witnessing the event could explain Fan Yu’s present condition.

Chen Ge frowned at the tabletop, then opened the black phone to review School of the Afterlife’s side missions. The description of Side Mission 6, Deep Well, read: ‘A brother and sister went to school. Why did neither return?’

The black phone did not make mistakes. What, then, did the siblings have to do with Fan Yu’s parents? Its hint implied that the brother and sister had fallen into the well, not the missing couple. How could both stories be true?

Chen Ge put the black phone away and looked at the woman with tears in her eyes. He asked with uncertainty, “Is Fan Yu an only child? Does he have brothers or sisters?”

The moment he asked, the woman’s expression changed. Her nails dug into her skin, and tears spilled down her face. “If that accident hadn’t taken my two children, Xiao Yu would have had a brother and sister to play with.”

“Your children?” Before Chen Ge entered the room, he had noticed that the clothes hanging on the rods outside were mostly women’s and children’s, so he had assumed the woman was not married.

“They died very young. They were only toddlers.” On the verge of breaking down, the woman stammered an apology and fled to the kitchen to compose herself.

So Fan Yu did have a brother and sister, but his aunt says they died years ago as toddlers. Why would the black phone say the siblings never returned from school? Toddlers don’t attend school. Is the phone wrong? Is the woman lying? Or did Fan Yu imagine something?

The woman remained in the kitchen. Chen Ge rose and headed toward the home’s only other room. Fan Yu should be inside, at the center of the entire mystery.

Chen Ge pushed open the door and entered an immaculate bedroom. Fan Yu stood at a table, apparently writing. When Chen Ge looked over his shoulder, he saw that the boy was drawing exclusively in black and red.

“Xiao Yu, what are you drawing?” Afraid that he might spook the boy, Chen Ge spoke in a soft voice. The boy turned to look at Chen Ge but did not answer. He turned back to focus on his drawing.

As Fan Yu added more color, the image took shape.

Several tiny red figures stood inside a pitch-black house.

After finishing the drawing, the boy crumpled the paper up and threw it onto the floor before starting a new drawing.

Chen Ge studied the drawings. Every one contained the same two elements: a black house and tiny red people.

What is he trying to convey?Chen Ge picked up the finished drawing from the floor and flattened it out. After studying it for some time, he silently slid it inside his pocket.
